_comment: Round 14, FINAL. The CORRECTED class-variation set, built on the user's final S01 design. Round 13 was rejected ('they look like the Mac in the 80s, more like a plate armour than a mech machine') - see moss-mech-r13-failed.md for the diagnosis. The cause was the keep-list, not the model: round 13's keep-list said 'relaxed upright standing pose' and 'overlapping CURVED armour plates', and S01 is neither.
_whatChangedFromR13: 1. THE CAMERA IS NOW IN THE KEEP-LIST. S01 is a high three-quarter view looking DOWN at the machine. Round 13 never mentioned the camera, so the model used its default straight-on eye-level front view.

2. THE POSE IS NOW S01's POSE. Round 13 said 'relaxed upright standing pose with feet apart and arms lowered' - which is a direct instruction to stand upright, the opposite of S01's hunched prowling stance. It now says: hunched, torso pitched forward, head thrust forward and down between the raised shoulders, arms hanging down and forward, legs crouched and splayed wide.

3. PROPORTIONS ARE MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. 'about five and a half heads tall, short thick legs, a broad deep torso' - round 13's vague 'broad heavy frame' let the model use its own stocky-mannequin default.

4. THE PLATES ARE FLAT AND FACETED, NOT CURVED. Round 13 said 'overlapping curved armour plates' and got round overlapping discs - a knight's pauldron. S01's shoulder plates are flat angular faceted slabs flaring up and out.

5. THE HEAD IS COWLED, NOT A HELMET. 'small dark cowled head module thrust forward and low with a narrow dark visor and two amber optic eyes' - round 13 got a big humanoid helmet standing above the shoulders.

6. HARD-EDGED MATERIAL VOCABULARY. 'hard-edged bevelled steel armour, angular and faceted with sharp corners and no rounded moulded forms' + 'exposed black mechanical structure between the plates - hydraulic pistons, actuators, hose bundles and cable looms'. This is what kills the 80s plastic-appliance read.

7. THE NEGATIVE gained the new failure modes: upright posture, standing straight, plate armour, knight, medieval, samurai, action figure, toy, mannequin, smooth plastic, beige plastic, retro appliance, rounded discs, flat blank panels, human face, anime face.
_classHardwareRule: Class hardware must be built from the MACHINE'S OWN construction vocabulary - dark bevelled steel, black hardware, the same dusty finish. Round 13's 'bulky rectangular rangefinder pod with a big glass lens' came out as a grey appliance box with a camera lens, and 'a long horizontal row of small glass sensor lenses' came out as a chrome speaker grille. Both read as consumer product, not war machine. Now: 'a slim folded sensor mast... a narrow vertical column of dark hardware', 'a long cylindrical sighting pod... mounted on a short black bracket'.
_recipe: This file. Re-runnable end to end: same instructions, same seeds, same output names.

concepts.name: 01_sniper_mast
concepts.instruction: Change only the machine's upper back so that a slim folded sensor mast rises from it directly behind the head, a narrow vertical column of dark hardware with a small glass lens at its top. Keep the same high three-quarter front view from above with the camera looking down on the machine at a steep angle so the tops of its shoulders and its back are visible and the whole machine sits small in the frame with air around it. Keep its hunched prowling stance with the torso pitched forward, the head thrust forward and down between the raised shoulders, the arms hanging down and forward with heavy clenched grippers, and the short thick legs crouched and splayed wide with the broad feet planted far apart. Keep its compact dense proportions, about five and a half heads tall, short thick legs and a broad deep torso. Keep the hard-edged bevelled steel armour, angular and faceted with sharp corners and no rounded moulded forms, the overlapping flat angular shoulder slabs stepping down and out over the upper arms with rivet rows along their edges, the small dark cowled head module thrust forward and low with a narrow dark visor and two amber optic eyes, the exposed black mechanical structure between the plates - hydraulic pistons, actuators, hose bundles and cable looms - the clusters of short black tubes on the upper back, its matte weathered painted steel in muted rust-orange over dark charcoal structure, the fine panel lines and rivet rows, the chipped edges showing bare steel and the dust settled in the panel recesses, and the plain evenly lit silver-grey studio backdrop with a soft contact shadow unchanged.
